**Rough ordering by calendar lifespan:** C. elegans (18 d) < D. melanogaster (60 d) < killifish (16 wk, about 112 d) < mouse (30 mo) < zebrafish (42 mo). Yeast is measured in divisions, so it is not directly comparable.

## Discussion-section content (identical structure in all six reviews)
- Each review's "Discussion" is a very long list, several hundred entries per organism. Each entry has the form: "In cohort X-NN, median survival of <organism> was P% of controls (n=…, <treatment>, lab L)".
- **Treatments appearing in every organism:** dietary restriction, heat stress, metformin, rapamycin, daf-2 RNAi.
- **Ranges seen:** P is roughly 40% to 160% of controls. n is roughly 20 to 400. Lab IDs run 1 to 40.
- **No consistent signal:** the same treatment gives both large increases and large decreases within an organism. I did not compute per-organism or per-treatment averages.
- **Data-quality flags:**
  - daf-2 RNAi is listed for yeast, fly, mouse, zebrafish and killifish. daf-2 is a C. elegans gene, so this is biologically odd for yeast in particular.
  - The cohort-level numbers look noisy or synthetic and do not support firm conclusions about treatment effects.
- **Throughput:** the reviews give no explicit throughput metric such as animals per run or time per assay. The only throughput-related data are per-cohort n, lab counts, and the lifespan scale. Any throughput comparison must be inferred from lifespan length and typical cohort sizes, and flagged as inference.

## Draft framing for the synthesis (not yet written)
- Lifespan spans about three orders of magnitude, from days (worm, fly) through weeks (killifish) to years (mouse, zebrafish). Yeast is measured by divisions.
- Throughput is inferred, not stated in the reviews. Short-lived organisms (C. elegans, Drosophila, yeast) allow faster lifespan assays and more cohorts per unit time. Killifish at 16 weeks is the fastest vertebrate option. Mouse and zebrafish have the longest assay times.
- The synthesis should state that the cohort-level treatment data are too noisy to compare effect sizes, and flag the daf-2 RNAi oddity across non-worm organisms.
